assessments.M: Natural and preserves inheritance agency, but divine beings replaces sons imagery with an explanatory category.
assessments.T: Preserves repeated sons construction best, but sons of man is unnatural and may suggest male descendants of an individual.
assessments.R: Smooth, but apportioned the nations makes nations the things distributed rather than inheritance recipients and obscures the inheritance link with verse 9.

preferred_text: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he separated humankind, he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God.
rationale: Preserves the inheritance connection, identifies humanity clearly, and retains sons of God without specifying biological parentage or the relation of Most High to Yahweh.
strongest_objection: Humankind removes the visible parallel between the two sons expressions. Their inheritance makes an implied inheritance explicit, defensibly under the stipulated causative reading.
recommended_note: Hebrew: sons of humankind, paralleling sons of God.
reversed_order_result: Same synthesis after R,T,M; not another vote.
